questions.q: What does `product-catalog` depend on to serve its endpoints?
options: PaymentPro and the legacy inventory service
Only Postgres — it has no outbound calls to other services
The shipping carrier webhook
Another copy of checkout for failover
questions.explain: product-catalog is a thin, read-heavy REST API with a single dependency: Postgres. It makes no outbound calls to PaymentPro, inventory, or shipping — that's checkout's job.

questions.q: In what order does the `POST /checkout` workflow call its dependencies?
options: Charge PaymentPro, confirm inventory stock, then webhook the shipping carrier
Webhook the shipping carrier, confirm stock, then charge PaymentPro
Confirm stock with the legacy inventory service, charge the card via PaymentPro, then webhook the shipping carrier
All three calls fire at the same time with no order
questions.explain: checkout first confirms stock with the legacy inventory service, then charges the customer through PaymentPro, and only after a successful charge does it hand the order to the shipping carrier via webhook.

options: A shared static API key hardcoded in the service
OAuth2 client-credentials, exchanging credentials for a bearer token
Basic auth with a username and password
No authentication is required for PaymentPro
questions.explain: checkout authenticates to PaymentPro using OAuth2 client-credentials, obtaining a bearer token before making the charge request.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT a reason Northbridge Retail built product-catalog and checkout as two separate services?
options: They have different scaling needs — checkout spikes during flash sales
They can be deployed and released independently
A failure in one has a smaller blast radius on the other
Postgres can only be reached from one service at a time
questions.explain: There's no such Postgres limitation — both services can reach Postgres. The real reasons are different scaling needs, independent release cadence, and smaller blast radius.

questions.q: Which statement about the legacy inventory service is accurate?
options: It is one of the two services built in this capstone
It is an existing service running elsewhere that checkout calls as an upstream dependency
It replaces product-catalog in production
It is built fresh in Chapter 2 alongside product-catalog and checkout
questions.explain: The legacy inventory service already exists and runs elsewhere at Northbridge. This capstone does not build it — checkout simply calls it to confirm stock before completing an order.
